design_summary.purpose: Single-clock FPGA-friendly PWM LED demo for board bring-up that produces a visible breathing/fading LED pattern on one output LED.
design_summary.operating_model: The design uses the single board clock clk to run all sequential logic, free-runs an 8-bit PWM counter, updates an 8-bit duty-cycle register only on slow update ticks generated by a counter-based divider, and uses a direction bit to reverse the duty ramp at 0x00 and 0xFF so the LED brightness repeatedly fades up and down through PWM comparison.

external_interfaces.name: clk
external_interfaces.description: Single board clock input that clocks all sequential logic in the design.

external_interfaces.name: led
external_interfaces.description: Active-high LED output driven by the PWM compare result to create the breathing effect.

module_architecture.name: pwm_fpga_demo
module_architecture.role: Top-level RTL module and complete implementation container for the FPGA LED breathing demo.
responsibilities: Accept the single board clock input and use it for all sequential logic.
Generate a slow tick from a counter-based clock divider or equivalent synthesizable counter scheme.
Maintain an 8-bit PWM counter that advances every clock cycle.
Maintain an 8-bit duty-cycle register that is updated only on slow tick events.
Maintain a direction bit that reverses the ramp at minimum and maximum duty endpoints.
Drive the LED output from a deterministic PWM comparison of the PWM counter and duty-cycle register.
Remain fully synthesizable and compatible with Yosys/nextpnr open-source FPGA flows.
interface_notes: The module interface is fixed to clk as the only input and led as the only output.
No additional top-level ports, resets, hidden side effects, or vendor-specific interfaces are introduced.
The LED output is intended to be active-high at the RTL level; any board-level polarity handling belongs outside the RTL if needed.
ownership_notes: The slow divider, PWM counter, duty-cycle register, and direction bit are all owned internally by the top module.
The module owns the visible breathing behavior entirely through its internal sequential state and compare-based LED drive.
Board-specific starter constraints are external to RTL and are not part of this module definition.

data_flow_summary: clk advances the internal PWM counter continuously on every clock cycle.
A slow counter derives a visible update tick without creating a derived clock.
On each slow tick, the duty-cycle register steps up or down based on the direction bit.
When the duty-cycle register reaches 8'hFF, direction flips downward; when it reaches 8'h00, direction flips upward.

The LED output is the direct result of comparing the free-running PWM counter against the current duty-cycle register, producing a high-frequency PWM waveform whose average brightness changes slowly over time.

clock_reset_summary.clocking: Single synchronous clock domain only, using clk for all sequential logic. No derived clocks are created.
clock_reset_summary.reset_behavior: No dedicated top-level reset input is specified. The implementation shall define safe deterministic startup behavior for synthesis on the intended FPGA flow, with counters, duty-cycle register, and direction bit initialized to a known state where supported. If explicit initialization is not supported on a target, the design must still remain synthesizable and self-start into a valid breathing sequence without requiring manual intervention.

integration_notes: Starter pin constraints are board-specific and must be generated separately after board selection.
Use PCF for iCE40 boards and LPF for ECP5 boards.
Starter constraints are for demo bring-up only and must be reviewed before programming physical hardware.
The RTL output file name is pwm_fpga_demo.v.
The implementation must stay compatible with lint, Yosys synthesis, nextpnr place-and-route, timing review, and bitstream handoff.
No memories, vendor primitives, ASIC-only constructs, delays, real-number types, DPI, or testbench-only code belong in the top module.
consistency_notes: Hierarchy, ports, and filenames are inherited from digital_spec_json.
